Fix option merging rewriting nested user data and flattening class instances

Deep merging recursed into any object value. Nested user data whose keys matched option names was rewritten as if it were options, and a class instance provided both as an instance default and again per request or via `.extend()` was merged into a plain object and lost its prototype. For example, an undici `Agent` passed as `dispatcher` ended up without `dispatch()`, and a `Date` inside `json` was sent as `{}`.

Only plain objects and arrays are merged now. Anything else replaces the parent value.

Fix `json` option keeping the content-type inherited from a `Request` input body

A `Request` input constructed with a body gets an automatic `text/plain;charset=UTF-8` content-type. That header was merged in before the `json` option set its own, so the JSON body was sent with the wrong content-type. Only a content-type explicitly passed via `options.headers` now takes precedence over `application/json`.
summary: Fixed later by 224034d: Fix headers set to `undefined` in `init` hooks being sent as the string `"undefined"`

request:
Fix headers set to `undefined` in `init` hooks being sent as the string `"undefined"`

Headers modified by `init` hooks skip the option merging that filters `undefined` values, and the `Headers` constructor turns `undefined` into the string `'undefined'`, so `options.headers.foo = undefined` in an `init` hook sent `foo: undefined` instead of removing the header. Plain header objects are now applied entry by entry so `undefined` deletes the header, matching the documented behavior for `.extend()`.

The check for a user-provided `Content-Type` had the same problem: it built a `Headers` instance from the raw header object, so removing the header in an `init` hook counted as providing one and the JSON body was sent without `application/json`. The check now uses the same header merging as the request.
summary: Fix headers set to `undefined` in `init` hooks being sent as the string `"undefined"`

Fix `Request` input body being dropped when using `searchParams`

The request was recreated from the normalized options to apply the new URL, but those options carry no body for a `Request` input, so the body was silently lost and the server received an empty request.

The input body is now carried over as a stream, which requires request stream support.
summary: Fixed later by 4e0bf0b: Fix `searchParams` dropping request options inherited from a `Request` input

request:
Fix `searchParams` dropping request options inherited from a `Request` input

When `searchParams` is set, the request is rebuilt with the new URL from the options alone, so `credentials`, `cache`, `redirect`, `integrity`, `referrer`, and `referrerPolicy` set on a `Request` input were reset to their defaults. In browsers this silently stopped sending cookies for `credentials: 'include'` requests. The rebuilt request now reads those options back from the request that was already constructed, so inherited values survive and explicit options still win.

fix(query-core): start queued scoped mutations while the window is not focused 🤖🤖🤖 (#11679)

fix(query-core): start queued scoped mutations while the window is not focused

A mutation queued behind another one in the same scope is started later
through retryer.continue(), which only resumes when canContinue() is true.
canContinue() requires the window to be focused, so with an unfocused tab
the next mutation stayed paused until the window got focus again.

Resume the initial start pause with canStart() instead, which is the same
check used to start the retryer right away. Retry pauses still use
canContinue().

Fixes #11642

* fix(query-core): resolve suspense when query data is set programmatically

When useSuspenseQuery is used and setQueryData populates the cache
while a fetch is in-flight, the suspense boundary stays stuck on the
original fetch promise. This prevents streamedQuery and manual cache
updates from releasing suspense.

Modify fetchOptimistic in queryObserver to use Promise.race between
the fetch promise and a cache subscriber that listens for 'updated'
events. When data appears in the cache via setQueryData or a streamed
chunk, the race resolves immediately without aborting the fetch.
This allows the suspense boundary to release and show the available
data while the fetch continues in the background.

Closes #10924

* fix(preact-query): retry on mount for falsy errors when throwOnError returns false

`ensurePreventErrorBoundaryRetry` only evaluated a function-valued
`throwOnError` when `query.state.error` was truthy. For a query that
rejected with a falsy value (e.g. `undefined`), the callback was skipped
and the function itself was treated as truthy, so `retryOnMount` was
disabled even though `throwOnError` would have returned `false`.

Check `query.state.status === 'error'` instead so the callback runs for
every failed query. Ports #11328 to preact-query.

fix: remove exponential backtracking from the emoji regex (#6347)

`\p{Extended_Pictographic}` and `\p{Emoji_Component}` overlap on U+1F9B0-U+1F9B3,
so `^(A|B)+$` had to re-explore 2^n ways of attributing the consumed characters
whenever the overall match failed. A ~100 byte string of those code points
followed by any non-emoji character stalled the event loop for seconds; each
additional character roughly doubled it.

Collapsing the alternation into a single character class matches exactly the same
set of strings — verified over every code point — and recheck reports it linear.
Same shape as the email regex fix in #2824.

The `redos checker` test only covered the date/time patterns, and it passed an
empty flags string, which makes recheck read `\p{...}` as a literal and report an
exponential pattern as safe. It moves to redos.test.ts, sweeps every pattern
core/regexes.ts exports, and passes the real flags.

Note that this changes the `pattern` emitted by `z.toJSONSchema(z.emoji())`.

Today a cyclic input is a RangeError, safeParse included, so it isn't
even catchable through the result.

Core gains a $ZodMemoizer seam: a container asks the injected memoizer
for the object it is about to build into. Classic injects one per
container instance; zod/mini injects nothing and links none of this.
Core's whole share is one interface, one `_zod` field, one changed

unless a layer asks for it. It registers the real output object before

fix(v4): keep a memoized node's cached issues private to the cache (#6443)

An issue belongs to the payload it was raised into, and every receiver prefixes
a path onto it in place. The memoizer handed the same issue objects to every
visitor of a shared node, so the second visitor prefixed onto the first one's
path: a DAG-shaped input reaching one invalid node twice reported
["right","left","name"] twice instead of ["left","name"] and ["right","name"].

Only the jitless object path is affected today, because the object JIT copies
each issue before prefixing it and util.prefixIssues does not.
